answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost.
